## Overview

1. Create Grid for defined boundary area (as per most suitable format)
2. Retrieve OSM layer data

These layers are required:
- Buildings
- Landuse
- Railways
- Roads
- Traffic
- Transport
- Water
- Waterways

Each layer should be split by its fclass or type to count the specific unique feature length/area in each grid cell

3. Filter OSM data to select specific layers and split by fclass
4. Clean overlapping features
5. Calculate total size of each feature (either length or area)
6. Intersect with grid
7. Calculate the area of each feature in each grid cell (either length or area)
8. Calculate the percentage of element in each grid cell
9. Package result in CSV with WKT geometry (EPSG 4326)

### Notes draft script 2022.07.05

- Discuss the fclass partitions. An fclass like 'building' for an area like London can have as much as 317 classes. Does it worth to partition the data in so many classes. Perhaps it is better to choose top N and recode 'others'
- An area like London is tessellated in more than 12 million hexagons
- See summary by 'layer'. What geometries to select? Is removing NA a valid approach?

Predominantly 'Way' types (ref: https://taginfo.openstreetmap.org/keys/building#overview):
- Buildings
- Landuse
- Water

multipolygons : “way” features that are recognized as area
lines : “way” features that are recognized as non-area.

'Way' features can be recognised as having area (ref: https://gdal.org/drivers/vector/osm.html) and are of layer type 'multipolygons'

## Process alphanumeric variables

```{r}
# ref function creation: https://mran.microsoft.com/snapshot/2017-09-15/web/packages/dplyr/vignettes/programming.html
# this function takes an sf dataframe, a key name and an h numerical to obtain a character of h highest values by key

values <- function(df, key, h) {
  
  qkey <- enquo(key)
  
  df %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    filter(!is.na(!!qkey)) %>%
    group_by(!!qkey) %>%
    count() %>%
    arrange(desc(n)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    slice_head(n = h) %>%
    pull(!!qkey) 
}

values_k <- values(mpg, landuse, 5)
```

```{r}
# recode to 'other' values that are not in highest occurrences
# this function takes an sf dataframe, a key name and to recode to 'other' those values that are not in the h highest values. 
# resulting sf has only the selected key name

recother <- function(df, key) {
  
  qkey <- enquo(key)
  
  df %>%
    filter(!is.na(!!qkey)) %>%
    mutate(!!qkey := case_when(!!qkey %in% values_k ~ !!qkey,
                               TRUE ~ "other")) %>%
    select(!!qkey)
}

recother(mpg, landuse) -> mpg_r
```

## Process geometries

```{r}
# ids of invalids geometries
which(st_is_valid(mpg_r, reason = TRUE) != "Valid Geometry") -> invalid
invalid
```

```{r}
# plot an example of invalid geometry
mpg_r["112",] %>%
  plot(max.plot = 1)
```

```{r}
# remove invalid geometries
mpg_r %>%
  slice(-invalid) -> mpg_r

# get only the non-empty geometries
mpg_r[!st_is_empty(mpg_r),, drop=FALSE] -> mpg_r
```


## Create hexagonal grid

```{r}
# bbox of London, layer = "multipolygons"
mpg %>%
  st_bbox() %>%
  st_as_sfc() %>%
  st_sf() %>%
  st_transform(crs = 4326) -> mpbox
```

```{r}
# create h3 hexagon grid at level 12 over the bbox of administrative area
h3_indexes <- polyfill(mpbox, res = 12)
# 12,015,189 hexagons

# # all hexagons ~ 12 GB
# h3_indexes %>%
#   h3_to_geo_boundary_sf() -> all_hex
```

### Study area from hex id

```{r}
# get hex id from: https://wolf-h3-viewer.glitch.me/
# hex id granary square
gsid <- "8c195da4d98b7ff"

# Get all neighbours within N steps of the hexagon from gsid
k_ring(gsid, radius = 11) %>%
  h3_to_geo_boundary_sf() %>%
  mutate(hexid = k_ring(gsid, radius = 11)) -> gshex
```

```{r}
# bbox of gshex as polygon
gshex %>%
  st_bbox() %>%
  st_as_sfc() %>%
  st_sf() %>%
  st_transform(crs = 4326) -> gsbox
```

```{r}
# cookie cut multipolygons in Granary Square area
st_crop(mpg_r, gsbox) -> gspol
```

```{r}
# intersect hexagons with buildings
st_intersection(gshex, gspol) -> hp_int
```

```{r}
# create multipolygons statistics by hexagon = landuse
hp_int %>%
  # calculate area
  mutate(area = as.numeric(st_area(.))) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  # classes areas as variables
  pivot_wider(names_from = "landuse", values_from = "area", values_fn = sum, values_fill = 0) -> hp_int_j

hp_int_j %>%
  # add prefix to columns 2 onwards
  rename_with( ~ paste0("l_", .x), .cols = 2:ncol(.)) %>%
  mutate_all( ~ replace(., is.na(.), 0)) %>%
  # add total
  mutate(total = rowSums(.[2:ncol(.)])) %>%
  # add percentage by column
  mutate_at(vars(starts_with("l")) , funs(pc = ./total * 100)) -> hp_int_j1
```

```{r}
# join statistics to hexagons
gshex %>%
  left_join(hp_int_j1, by="hexid") -> gshexsum
```

```{r}
plot(gshexsum[,c("l_grass", "l_other", "total")])
```

```{r}
mapview(gspol) + mapview(gshexsum, zcol = "total")
```

## Export csv
```{r}
st_write(gshexsum, "csv/gshexsum_wkt_landuse_studyarea.csv", layer_options = c("GEOMETRY=AS_WKT","CREATE_CSVT=YES"), delete_dsn=TRUE)
```
